item.title: Anthropic S-1 Breakdown (Kepler)
item.description: A line-by-line reading of the first financial statements ever published by a frontier AI lab, with every figure linked back to the filing: how compute is contracted 12-18 months ahead and expensed as capacity comes online, why an $80.7 billion half-year loss is mostly a non-cash accounting mark on convertible notes, and what roughly $600 billion in compute agreements and leased data centres mean for the company's cash. Makes the economics of a frontier lab concrete. Prepared from the public filing by a research firm that uses Claude in its product.

item.title: Formalizing the Enormous Theorem (Axiom)
item.description: The team's own account of how a swarm of AI agents, steered by a handful of mathematicians, turned the 15,000-page Classification of Finite Simple Groups (the 'periodic table' of symmetry, built by over 100 mathematicians across decades) into about 43 million lines of machine-checked Lean in 24 days: how the proof was cut into 108 milestones and 380 tasks, where unproved assumptions crept in and had to be ripped out, the gap they found and rerouted, and the 34 deviations from the published literature. A first-hand look at AI doing mathematics at a scale no human team could check.

item.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (He et al., 2015)
item.description: The most-cited paper of the century: skip connections made very deep networks trainable, and they're in every modern architecture.
